clue.text: Examines old boat, say, getting a bit detached?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for examines is to be heard, giving a same-sounding banking word

parts.note: examines means checks, which sounds like the paper payment orders
a tub is an old or clumsy boat

explanation.surface: Someone inspects an ancient vessel and finds a piece of it has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear CHECKS (Examines) as CHEQUES; add TUB. The question mark flags that the counterfoil is the bit left behind when the cheque itself is detached.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfoil is the record kept when the payment slip is torn away, so it is the remnant of a detached piece.

clue.text: Instrument needs altering in different places

indicators.note: putting letters in different places means rearranging the word altering

explanation.surface: A musical instrument has to be modified at several points.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument: a steel bar bent into a three-sided shape and struck with a beater.

clue.text: He wrote the Ancient Mariner

parts.note: Alexander Pope, the eighteenth-century poet, is a man who wrote
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A quiz answer naming the poet of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites Coleridge, but 'He wrote' is any writer, here POPE, and 'the Ancient' is YE; the sailor is the cartoon one.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating cartoon character is a sailor, and a mariner is a seaman.

clue.text: A wife abandons puzzle and dances

indicators.note: abandons says the letters for a wife leave the word for the puzzle

parts.note: a jigsaw is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: A wife gives up on a puzzle and goes dancing instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively folk dances in triple time, often Scottish or Irish, are called by this name.

clue.text: Scots trick one of their own, holding a light

indicators.note: holding means the first letters keep the next pieces inside them

parts.note: to con is to trick
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, one of the Scots' own

explanation.surface: Scots play a trick on a fellow Scot who is carrying a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of their own' means a typically Scottish name, which is why IAN fits here. 'holding' puts the light inside, straight after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so the adjective means Scottish.

clue.text: Pompous type had one curry sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
dhal is an Indian lentil curry

explanation.surface: A self-important person ate a curry, and was mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses HAD I DHAL; in a down entry it reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A snobbish affected person is mocked with this phrase imitating posh speech.

clue.text: Cross line leaving for take-off

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for line departs from the word for the cross

parts.note: a saltire is a diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag

explanation.surface: An angry flight passenger crosses the queue on the way to departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the St Andrew's cross, SALTIRE, which loses L.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a mocking imitation, which is what lampooning work does.

clue.text: It's played very loudly around one eastern county

indicators.note: around means the musical marking wraps round the following letters

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instrument is being played at full volume somewhere in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's played' is a second hint: the small flute of the same name. FIFE is a Scottish county.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish region north of Edinburgh across the Forth was historically a county.

clue.text: Play this on 1 March badly, then 1 April

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the 1 before April means its first letter only, its number one letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to play an instrument on two dates, poorly the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ON + I + MARCH; '1 April' gives the first letter of April.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is an instrument you play, so this is something to play.

clue.text: Fiddle in the morning at 1

parts.note: am stands for ante meridiem, before noon
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A violin is being played at one in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made fine violins, so their instruments are fiddles.

clue.text: Question states: "Should these be sung with tremolo?"

definitions.text: Should these be sung with tremolo?

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A query on whether singers should add vibrato.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: musical notes, and the verb for trilling or trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: These are eighth notes in music, and to tremble or trill in voice is also expressed by this word.

clue.text: Last part learned in upright position

parts.note: the end is the last part
learned means wise

explanation.surface: The final section of a lesson was learnt while standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed with an end upward or forward, i.e. standing on its tip, is the dictionary sense.

clue.text: European composer nearly withdraws good score, of course

indicators.note: withdraws means draws back, so the letters are read backwards
nearly means the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer

explanation.surface: A European composer pulls out of a match with a good result, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ELGAR to ELGA, which 'withdraws' reverses to AGLE. 'of course' means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, two strokes under par for a hole is a fine score.

clue.text: Clan wars overwhelm Cornish resort, as Spooner has it?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade first sounds

parts.note: to flood is to overwhelm
Bude is a seaside resort town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: Tribal conflict swamps a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of FLOOD BUDE and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running vendetta between families or clans is a deadly quarrel of this kind.

clue.text: Say catchphrase over in pub that's used by climbers

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters sit inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
a motto is a catchphrase or slogan

explanation.surface: Mountaineers in a pub repeat their favourite saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns round the whole of the example-plus-slogan string, and 'in' sets it inside the pub. The climbers are vehicles going up hills, not mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest ratio in a vehicle's gearbox is used when climbing steep slopes.

clue.text: Maybe peck seed Murray ground

indicators.note: ground, as grain is milled, means these letters are broken down and remade

explanation.surface: A bird perhaps picks at seed that Murray has milled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peck' looks like a bird's action; it is a unit, a quarter of a bushel.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck is an example of a unit for grain and other dry goods.

clue.text: Euphemistic drama, terribly hot physical test

indicators.note: terribly means the letters are badly treated, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A play that hides its name proves to be a gruelling, sweaty endurance trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors superstitiously avoid naming Macbeth in the theatre, using this euphemism instead.

clue.text: Edit article about new liquorice stick

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for new
edit means the word article is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer revises a piece about a new sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edit' rearranges ARTICLE, and 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz slang calls the black woodwind instrument a liquorice stick for its look.

clue.text: Rowdies touring in Spain see dirty jumpers here

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rowdies' letters surround the next ones

parts.note: louts are rowdy people
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Hooligans on tour in Spain spot grubby sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like sweaters; they are rugby players leaping for the ball, muddy from the game.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, players leap to catch the ball thrown in from touch at these restarts.

clue.text: Almost all soldiers in a group love performing musical

indicators.note: almost all means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a brigade is a large group of soldiers
love is zero in tennis, O
on stage, performing, is on

explanation.surface: Almost every soldier in a unit loves putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage show about a Scottish village appearing once a century.

clue.text: Around noon, radio broadcast raid

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the letter for noon
broadcast means scattered, so the word radio is rearranged

explanation.surface: About midday, a wireless reports an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion or attack into enemy territory is a raid.

clue.text: Queen takes in one orphan

indicators.note: takes in means the queen's name holds the next letter inside

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Britain 1702-14
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A queen adopts a parentless child.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical heroine without parents.

clue.text: Charioteer drivers carrying superior gear

indicators.note: carrying means the drivers' letters hold the next pieces

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
U means upper class, superior
rig is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Chariot drivers carry first-rate equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern constellation bears the Latin name for a charioteer.

clue.text: Game played in the Dog and Fish

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A game played in a pub called the Dog and Fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dog and Fish reads as a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish ice sport of sliding stones towards a target.

clue.text: Show around back street

parts.note: ca, circa, means around

indicators.note: back means the word for street is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An exhibit is around the back street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber stage musical is an example of a show.

clue.text: Clansmen continue south, crossing road

indicators.note: crossing means the word for continue lies across, so around, the road letters

parts.note: go on means continue

explanation.surface: Scottish clan members keep heading south over the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a famous Highland clan, also the Highlanders regiment.

clue.text: In which to see drivers turn left in odd places

parts.note: a go is a turn

indicators.note: in odd places means taking only the first and third letters of left

explanation.surface: Motorists are told to steer left at strange points.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a long club used in this sport, so it is where such clubs appear.

clue.text: Old landowner's article defending origins of art nouveau

indicators.note: defending means the article surrounds and protects the next letters

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: origins of means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A historic property owner's essay champions the decorative style.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scotland, a clan chief or lord holding land from the king bore this title, as Macbeth did.

clue.text: Hide supplier at rebuilt gorilla cages

indicators.note: cages means the rearranged letters enclose the word at
rebuilt means the word gorilla is put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A provider of animal skins is at the zoo while gorilla enclosures are reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile's skin is tanned as leather, so it supplies a hide.
